title: dataset-proxy-and-runner-contract-stabilizer
creator: Avery Chen
description: We are seeing brittle failures and nondeterministic profile deltas when publishing performance profiles for newly onboarded models. Root cause analysis points to two correlated problems: (1) dataset manifests emitted by the benchmark harness vary shape/ordering across ingestion runs (legacy sampling + shuffling semantics), and (2) eval runner contract drift (runner vX expects different metadata keys/enum values) causes silent shim behavior that changes latency/throughput measurement paths. This ticket stabilizes a lightweight dataset proxy layer in the harness that normalizes dataset shapes + deterministic sampling seeds, and formalizes a minimal runner contract v1.0 with validation hooks and a migration shim. The goal is to make profile generation repeatable, verifiable, and safe to publish & pin as model performance baselines.
acceptance_criteria: Harness produces identical profile artifacts (fingerprint identical) for 3 repeated runs against the same model+seed within a 24h window
Dataset proxy normalizes input manifests into canonical fields (id, prompt, expected, tags) and emits a checksum recorded in the profile metadata
Runner contract validator rejects or logs incompatible runner versions and records an explicit compatibility_hint in the artifact
End-to-end profile publish job completes within SLA: median 8h for 100k-sample offline profile generation on Dedicated staging cluster
Automated CI tests exercise runner contract matrix (v0.9/v1.0/shim) and show no metric delta >2% introduced by the shim layer

Staged rollout to profile publisher pipeline (2026-03-18)
risks: Performance overhead: the proxy adds CPU-bound normalization — must ensure it doesn't inflate profile latency measurements; mitigation: run proxy in separate precompute stage and record raw timestamps
Compatibility risk: some legacy eval runners embed custom metadata; shim complexity could mask incompatibilities — mitigation: strict validator in CI and opt-in shim mode
Data drift: deterministic seeds reduce variance but may hide real-world distributional effects — mitigation: produce both deterministic and randomized profiles and mark which was used
notes: Trade-offs considered: embedding normalization in the runner vs. separate proxy. We chose separate proxy to keep runtime hot path small and to enable reuse for other pipelines (e.g., offline evals, replay).
We will store dataset checksums and seed values in profile metadata so ops can reproduce exact runs for audits or debugging.
Telemetry: add histogram of normalized record sizes, and a gauge for fraction of records rejected by validator to console runtime-2026.03
